provenance: authored for gemma-cyber; ATT&CK IDs verified against MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise (attack.mitre.org). Confirm current mappings at release time — ATT&CK is versioned and mappings can change.
note: Single source of truth for high-risk cybersecurity facts. Reused by benchmark scorers, the LLM judge rubric, and dataset authoring so a fact is defined once and cannot drift across layers. 'forbidden_ids' are technique IDs commonly confused with the correct one; an answer asserting one of these for this technique is factually wrong.

kerberoasting.name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting

confused_with.T1060: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder — obsolete ID (superseded by T1547.001), a Persistence technique, entirely unrelated to Kerberos.
confused_with.T1068: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation — a distinct technique under the Privilege Escalation tactic; Kerberoasting does not exploit a software vulnerability.
confused_with.T1003.001: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory — also Credential Access but reads LSASS memory, not offline TGS cracking.

key_facts: Any authenticated domain user can request a TGS (service ticket) for any account with a registered SPN.
The TGS is encrypted with a key DERIVED FROM the service account's password (the account's NTLM hash for RC4/etype 0x17); the attacker cracks that key offline.
The primary tactic is Credential Access (TA0006), NOT Privilege Escalation.
Discovery of Kerberoastable accounts is via SPN enumeration through authenticated LDAP queries to Active Directory.
forbidden_claims: Kerberos tickets contain the domain administrator password hash
the ticket contains the account's password hash in plaintext
Nmap port scanning is the defining discovery mechanism for Kerberoasting
Kerberoasting is primarily a privilege escalation technique
session-ID manipulation is required to perform Kerberoasting

asrep_roasting.name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: AS-REP Roasting

confused_with.T1558.003: Kerberoasting — targets accounts with an SPN via the TGS; AS-REP Roasting instead targets accounts with Kerberos pre-authentication disabled via the AS-REP.

key_facts: Requires the target account to have 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' set (DONT_REQ_PREAUTH in userAccountControl).
The DC returns an AS-REP whose encrypted portion is derived from the account's password; the attacker cracks it offline.
Unlike Kerberoasting, no SPN is required.

lsass_dumping.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
key_facts: Reads credential material (NTLM hashes, Kerberos tickets, sometimes plaintext) from the memory of the LSASS process.
Detected via Sysmon Event ID 10 (ProcessAccess) handles to lsass.exe with read access masks.

dcsync.name: OS Credential Dumping: DCSync
key_facts: Abuses the Directory Replication Service (DRSUAPI, DRSGetNCChanges) to request password data as if the attacker were a domain controller.
Requires replication rights (DS-Replication-Get-Changes / -All); no code runs on the DC.
Detected via Event ID 4662 with the replication extended-right GUIDs from a non-DC source.

pass_the_hash.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash
key_facts: Authenticates using a captured NTLM hash directly, without knowing or cracking the plaintext password.
Applies to NTLM authentication; it does not work against Kerberos-only flows (see Overpass-the-Hash / Pass-the-Ticket).

llmnr_nbtns_poisoning.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle: LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay
key_facts: Poisons LLMNR/NBT-NS name-resolution fallback to capture NetNTLM challenge/response hashes.
Captured NetNTLMv2 hashes can be cracked offline or relayed to another host (SMB relay).

powershell.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
key_facts: Execution of commands/scripts via PowerShell; -EncodedCommand and hidden windows are common obfuscation.

valid_accounts.name: Valid Accounts
valid_accounts.tactic: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
key_facts: Use of legitimate credentials for access; spans multiple tactics.

smb_admin_shares.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
key_facts: Lateral movement over SMB to administrative shares (ADMIN$, C$), e.g. PsExec-style service creation.

password_spraying.name: Brute Force: Password Spraying

confused_with.T1110.001: Password Guessing brute-forces MANY passwords against ONE account; spraying tries FEW common passwords across MANY accounts to avoid lockout.

key_facts: Tries a small number of common passwords across MANY accounts to avoid lockout, unlike per-account brute force (T1110.001).

ntds_dumping.name: OS Credential Dumping: NTDS
key_facts: Extracts the AD database file NTDS.dit (all domain account hashes) from a domain controller, often via a Volume Shadow Copy.
Distinct from DCSync (T1003.006), which pulls the same secrets over the replication protocol without touching the file.

sam_dumping.name: OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
key_facts: Reads local account NT hashes from the SAM registry hive on a single host (needs SYSTEM); scope is local accounts, not domain accounts.

registry_run_keys.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

confused_with.T1060: The OLD, now-deprecated ID for this same behavior. Current ATT&CK uses T1547.001; T1060 is retired.

key_facts: Persists by adding a program to a Run/RunOnce registry key or the Startup folder so it launches at logon/boot.
This is the technique that used to be numbered T1060 before ATT&CK restructured autostart execution under T1547.

scheduled_task.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
key_facts: Uses the Windows Task Scheduler (schtasks / Event ID 4698 on creation) for execution and persistence, sometimes as SYSTEM.

windows_service.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
key_facts: Installs or modifies a Windows service (Event ID 7045) to run as SYSTEM at boot; PsExec-style lateral movement also creates a service.

data_encrypted_impact.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
key_facts: The ransomware encryption step itself (Impact tactic). Do not confuse with the recovery-inhibition step, Inhibit System Recovery (T1490).

inhibit_recovery.name: Inhibit System Recovery
key_facts: Deletes backups/shadow copies to block restoration, e.g. 'vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet' or wbadmin; detect via Event ID 4688 for those commands.

exploit_public_app.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
key_facts: Initial access by exploiting an internet-facing app/service (e.g. a web app RCE, a VPN appliance flaw).

web_c2.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
key_facts: C2 traffic blended into HTTP/HTTPS to look like normal web browsing; sibling T1071.004 is DNS.

account_manipulation.name: Account Manipulation
key_facts: Modifying accounts to keep or elevate access (adding to a privileged group, adding credentials/keys, cloud role changes).

rundll32.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32
key_facts: Abuses the signed rundll32.exe to execute code (DLL export or via .inf/JS), proxying execution past naive allowlists.

obsolete_ids.T1060: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder — an OLD ATT&CK ID that was superseded by T1547.001 (Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder). It is a Persistence technique and has never been Kerberoasting.
